title: Daehan Dawon Tea Plantation: Korea's Most Famous Green Tea Fields in Boseong (Beginner's Guide)
html:
If you search "Korea green tea" online, odds are good you'll see a photo of curved green rows climbing a hillside — and that photo is almost always Daehan Dawon Tea Plantation (대한다원) in Boseong, a county on Korea's southern coast famous for growing green tea. It's a few hours from Seoul and not somewhere most first-time visitors plan ahead, but if you love photogenic landscapes — or you're building a longer trip around South Jeolla Province — it's worth the detour.

Why Everyone Knows This Place

Daehan Dawon is one of the biggest tea plantations in Korea, and its rows of tea bushes are planted in long, curved lines that follow the shape of the hill — which is exactly why it photographs so well. The entrance path is lined with tall Japanese cedar trees planted close together, so you walk through a cool, shaded tunnel before the tea fields even come into view. The plantation has also shown up as a filming location in several popular Korean dramas, including Legend of the Blue Sea (2017) and Summer Scent (2002), so don't be surprised if it looks familiar even on your first visit.

What to Do Once You're There

The whole visit is really just a walk — you're not paying for a specific activity, just the chance to wander the grounds. From the observation deck near the top of the hill (the plantation sits at about 350 meters above sea level), you can see rows of tea stretching out below you, and on a clear day, the sea in the distance. Give yourself at least an hour to walk around slowly, take photos, and enjoy the quiet — it's genuinely one of the most relaxing stops on a Korea itinerary.

💡 Local tip: Korean visitors usually stop for the green tea ice cream and green tea lattes sold near the entrance — it sounds like a tourist cliché, but the tea really is grown just up the hill, so locals say it tastes noticeably fresher than the green tea drinks you'll find in a Seoul convenience store.

Best Time of Year to Go

The tea bushes stay green all year (it's an evergreen plant), but the look of the plantation changes a lot with the seasons:

  • Late April to May — new leaves come in a brighter, lighter green, and this is around when the nearby Boseong Green Tea Festival (a local festival celebrating the tea harvest) usually takes place.
  • Summer — the deepest, darkest green of the year, and the cedar tunnel at the entrance is a welcome bit of shade from the heat.
  • Mid-January — a surprise favorite among Korean photographers: light snow sitting on the dark green rows makes for a striking contrast, and the area often runs a tea-field light festival nearby in winter too.

Hours, Admission, and Getting There

Daehan Dawon is open every day of the year, with no regular closed days. Hours run roughly 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. (a little later in peak summer, a little earlier in winter), and there's a small admission fee — around ₩4,000 for adults, less for students, seniors, and young children. Exact hours and prices can shift a little by season, so if you're planning to arrive right at opening or closing time, it's worth a quick call to +82-61-852-4540 to confirm first.

Boseong doesn't have its own KTX (Korea's high-speed train) station, so getting there takes a bit of planning:

  • From Seoul, the simplest option for first-timers is the direct intercity bus from Seoul's Central City Terminal (in Gangnam) to Boseong Bus Terminal — about 4 hours 40 minutes, with only a couple of departures a day, so book your seat ahead of time through a bus-booking app or at the terminal.
  • Alternatively, take the KTX to Gwangju-Songjeong or Suncheon, then switch to a local bus or train onward to Boseong.
  • From Boseong Bus Terminal, a local bus heading toward "Dawon" or "녹차밭" (green tea field) — or a short 15–20 minute taxi ride — will get you to the plantation gate.

Because the round trip from Seoul takes most of a day, this is best treated as a stop on a longer South Jeolla itinerary — pairing it with nearby Suncheon Bay or the mudflat town of Beolgyo (famous for its cockle dishes) makes for a fuller day out.

💬 Planning a trip down to Boseong? Let me know in the comments — happy to help you work it into your route!
meta_description: Boseong's famous green tea plantation: best season to visit, admission, hours, and how to get there from Seoul without a car.
